records.constraint: Write a lyric in a major key. Make it about something that hurts.
records.prompt: Pick a key — G, C, or D. Strum a happy chord progression. Now write words about a loss over those bright chords. Let the mismatch sit there.
records.payoff: Happy music over sad words creates something neither can alone. That tension is your song.

records.constraint: Write a riff that lands on beat 2 instead of beat 1.
records.prompt: Play a 4-beat pattern. Start your riff on beat 2, not beat 1. The kick drum hits first. Your riff answers it. Loop it until it grooves.
records.payoff: Starting on the offbeat makes the riff feel like it's chasing something. That's groove.

records.constraint: Tell a true story in exactly 4 lines. Each line is one sentence.
records.prompt: Think of something that happened to you. Beginning, middle, end, and one detail you still remember. Four sentences. That's the verse.
records.payoff: You just wrote a song verse. It was always that simple.

records.constraint: Hum a melody. Then play the same rhythm on muted strings.
records.prompt: Hum something — anything. Record it or just remember it. Now mute all strings and strum that exact rhythm. The rhythm IS the melody's skeleton.
records.payoff: Melody and rhythm are the same thing at different speeds. You just proved it.

records.constraint: Write a lyric. Play a riff that contradicts the mood.
records.prompt: Write a tender lyric — something soft and honest. Now play an aggressive riff over it. Don't soften the riff. Let them clash.
records.payoff: When gentle words meet harsh music, the listener has to decide what's real. That's engagement.

records.constraint: Tell a story using only rhythm. No pitch, no words.
records.prompt: Mute all strings. Strum a pattern: quiet parts = sad, loud parts = intense, pauses = dramatic. Tell the whole story with dynamics alone.
records.payoff: Rhythm carries emotion even without a single note. You just proved it.

records.constraint: Play a riff in E. Sing a melody in A over it.
records.prompt: Play a simple riff in the key of E. Now sing a melody in A — a different key. Don't resolve the clash. Let both exist together.
records.payoff: Two keys at once create a sound neither could alone. You just found a third harmony.

records.constraint: Speak a sentence out loud. That's your strum pattern.
records.prompt: Say a sentence — any sentence. Listen to the natural rhythm of the words. Now strum that exact pattern. Down for stressed syllables, up for unstressed.
records.payoff: You've been a rhythm player since you learned to talk. You just connected the two.

records.constraint: Sing a story using only vowels — ah, oh, ee. No words.
records.prompt: Pick a story — something that happened. Now sing it using only 'ah,' 'oh,' and 'ee.' The melody carries the emotion. No lyrics needed.
records.payoff: When words vanish, melody becomes the storyteller. You just proved music predates language.

records.constraint: Play a riff that sounds like a person you know.
records.prompt: Think of someone — their personality, their energy. Play a riff that matches them. Not their music. Them. Aggressive? Play aggressive. Nervous? Play nervous.
records.payoff: Riffs carry character. You just turned a person into a motif.

records.constraint: Record your heartbeat. Sing over it. Write words for it.
records.prompt: Put your phone on your chest. Record the pulse. Hum a melody over the loop. Now write words that fit the rhythm of your own heartbeat. The heartbeat is the foundation.
records.payoff: You just built a song from your own body. That's as personal as music gets.

records.constraint: Write 3 lines of story. Give each line a different riff.
records.prompt: Line 1: set the scene (play a riff). Line 2: the conflict (play a different riff). Line 3: the outcome (play a third riff). Write lyrics that connect them.
records.payoff: Riffs are chapters. You just scored a narrative with guitar.

records.constraint: Put the guitar down. Tell a story with your voice and body only.
records.prompt: No guitar. Clap, stomp, hum, sing. Tell a story using only your body. No instrument. Just you and rhythm.
records.payoff: You are the instrument. The guitar was always optional.

records.constraint: Write a riff. Sing a different melody over it. Write lyrics that match the melody, not the riff.
records.prompt: Build a riff. Now sing a melody that ignores the riff's mood. Write words that follow the melody's emotion, not the riff's. Three layers, three moods.
records.payoff: When layers disagree, the listener assembles the meaning. That's how complex songs work.

records.constraint: Write a riff with 3 notes. Match each note to a word.
records.prompt: Pick 3 notes on one string. Assign one word to each note. Now play the notes in order and say the words at the same time. That's your chorus.
records.payoff: You just built a hook from the ground up. Notes and words as one unit.

records.constraint: Play a riff. Sing a melody that starts where the riff ends.
records.prompt: Play a 2-bar riff. When it stops, start singing — pick up where the riff left off. The riff hands off to the melody like a relay baton.
records.payoff: Riff and melody can share one idea by taking turns. You just built a conversation.

records.constraint: Write a story in present tense. Sing it. No past tense allowed.
records.prompt: Write 4 lines about something happening RIGHT NOW. Not 'I went' — 'I'm going.' Not 'she said' — 'she says.' Sing it. Present tense makes it urgent.
records.payoff: Present tense pulls the listener into the moment. You just made a song that feels like now.

records.constraint: Mute all strings. Tell a story with rhythm. Then add ONE riff note.
records.prompt: Mute everything. Strum patterns for 30 seconds — quiet, loud, fast, slow. Now let ONE note ring out. That single note is the climax of your story.
records.payoff: One note after 30 seconds of rhythm hits harder than anything you've ever played.

records.constraint: Layer a loop: rhythm first, then riff, then melody, then words. Never go back and change.
records.prompt: Record rhythm (30 sec). Record riff on top (30 sec). Record melody on top (30 sec). Write words over everything (30 sec). Each layer is permanent. No editing.
records.payoff: Constraints breed creativity. You can't fix it — so you make it work.

records.constraint: Write a complete song in 10 minutes. All four layers. Start now.
records.prompt: Timer: 10 minutes. Pick a key. Play a riff. Hum a melody. Write words. The song doesn't need to be good. It needs to be finished.
records.payoff: Your first instinct was better than your perfectionism. You just wrote a song.

records.constraint: No lyrics. Tell a story with melody, riff, and rhythm only.
records.prompt: No words. Hum, whistle, or scat the melody. Let the riff carry the attitude. Let rhythm carry the narrative. The story must make sense without a single word.
records.payoff: When words vanish, every other element has to work harder. You just made music speak without language.

records.constraint: Write a verse with slow rhythm. Write a chorus with fast rhythm. The tempo change IS the story.
records.prompt: Verse: slow strum, gentle words. Chorus: fast strum, louder words. The tempo shift is the plot twist. The story changes because the speed changes.
records.payoff: Tempo is narrative. You just used speed as a storytelling device.

records.constraint: Write a song in gibberish. The melody, rhythm, and story must still make sense.
records.prompt: No real words. Make up sounds. But the melody must carry emotion, the rhythm must carry narrative, and the listener must feel something. No hiding behind 'I don't know what I'm saying.'
records.payoff: If the feeling lands without language, you understand music at its deepest level.

records.constraint: Write a love song where the riff sounds angry.
records.prompt: Sweet lyrics. Sweet melody. Angry riff. The guitar doesn't believe the words. Let the listener decide who's telling the truth.
records.payoff: When the guitar disagrees with the singer, the song gets honest.

records.constraint: All five layers. 5 minutes. No preparation. Hit record now.
records.prompt: Record everything at once. Riff, rhythm, melody, words, story arc. Don't plan. Don't think. Just build. Whatever comes out IS the song.
records.payoff: This is what you sound like when you stop trying to be good. That's the most honest thing you've ever made.

records.constraint: Record everything. Listen back. Find the 3 seconds that feel real. Build around those.
records.prompt: Record a full take. Listen. Find the 3 seconds that made you feel something — even a flicker. Delete everything else. Build the whole song from those 3 seconds.
records.payoff: The song was always 3 seconds long. Everything else was scaffolding.

records.constraint: Play it for someone. Watch their face. The song is whatever made them react.
records.prompt: Play your song for someone — friend, stranger, anyone. Don't explain it. Watch their face. The moment they react? That's the real song.
records.payoff: Music isn't what you play — it's what lands.

records.constraint: Start with all five layers. Every 30 seconds, remove one. End with only lyrics and silence.
records.prompt: Start with everything playing. After 30 seconds, remove the riff. After another 30, remove the drums. Keep stripping until only your voice and silence remain.
records.payoff: The song teaches you what it was actually about by taking away everything it was hiding behind.

records.constraint: Make it sound like a celebration. The story must be about loss.
records.prompt: Upbeat riff. Bouncy rhythm. Soaring melody. Happy-sounding. But the words are about losing someone. Make the party feel like a funeral. Nobody at the party knows.
records.payoff: Joy and grief share a skeleton. The groove is the only thing keeping both upright.

records.constraint: Title the song first. Then write every element to contradict the title.
records.prompt: Pick a title: 'I'm Fine,' 'Nothing Hurts,' 'I'm Over It.' Now write the song that proves the title is a lie. Every element contradicts the title.
records.payoff: You discover how obvious a lie becomes when the band stops covering for it.

records.constraint: Use only one chord. One riff note. One rhythm. One image. Make it enough.
records.prompt: One chord. One note repeated in a riff. One rhythm pattern. One image in the lyrics. That's all you get. Make it enough.
records.payoff: The fewer tools you have, the more each one matters. You just learned that limitation is the mother of invention.

records.constraint: Every element must disagree with every other element for the whole song.
records.prompt: Lyrics say one thing. Melody says another. Riff says something else. Rhythm fights the riff. Story contradicts the lyrics. Nothing agrees. Make it work anyway.
records.payoff: The arrangement reveals the civil war your face concealed.
